(1) FLORA is an adequate language for the implementation of the physical WebBase layer and (2) the implementation of this layer is a challenging task that requires the use of a number of techniques, including the development of an extensible framework, the use of a declarative approach to the design and the use of a deductive system to implement the framework.
(1) FLORA is well suited for building XRover, (2) FLORA is a good choice for building other webbases, and (3) webbases are a good choice for many applications.
(1) FLORA is a good language for building webbases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing techniques and tools to support the creation of webbases.
building systems that enable users to easily access data from the Internet.
the development and evaluation of a deductive object oriented approach to building Webbases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design and implementation of the physical-layer of a Webbase system, such as XRover, is not a trivial task.

we have developed a prototype system that is able to automatically locate and extract dynamic data from Web pages and that we have developed the necessary technology for a webbase system to automatically build its own knowledge base.
XRover is a successful prototype of a webbase physical layer that is based on deductive object-oriented technology and is implemented using the FLORA-2 deductive database system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully demonstrated that the webbase architecture can be implemented using a deductive object- oriented database system.
the use of FLORA as the implementation language of the webbase physical layer has been a very successful experience.
the use of FLORA as the implementation language for XRover was a good choice.

FLORA provides a powerful and convenient environment for building XRover.
